scope: A production MarketDataFreshnessProbe (atp-orchestrator BoardFreshnessProbe) answered from a shared, thread-safe LineFreshnessBoard in atp-market-data that wraps SRS-MD-003's HeartbeatFreshnessMonitor (and, for providers with an upstream sequence, SRS-MD-007's SequenceGapDetector via combined_line_freshness), evaluated at read time on one clock: in production the operating system's suspend-inclusive monotonic clock (CLOCK_BOOTTIME on Linux, CLOCK_MONOTONIC on macOS, via the rustix crate); on a gap-tracked board only a tick carrying new data refreshes a line. The live order path (route_order and route_order_durably, through submit_live_order) and the paper order path (dispatch_order's InternalSimulation arm, new) consult it, so stale subscribed data blocks submissions with MARKET_DATA_STALE and fresh data resumes them. The port becomes security-aware (symbol + asset class) and age-honest (staleness_seconds: Option<u64>). Closes ERR-3's paper half. Does NOT feed the board from the live IB tick stream: composing the SRS-MD-003 feed loop into the live execution host is SRS-EXE-001's IB-tier wiring, so that tier stays refused.

obligations.criterion: Given a subscribed instrument whose combined line freshness from HeartbeatFreshnessMonitor is older than the 15 s staleness threshold, the production probe reports it stale; after a tick newer than the threshold it reports it fresh. Exercised with an injected clock, no sleeps. A duplicate or replayed tick on a gap-tracked board does not refresh a time-stale line, and a sequence-less refresh is refused there.

Given the probe reports an instrument stale, a live submission for it through route_order returns MARKET_DATA_STALE and the broker test double records zero submit calls; given it reports fresh, the same submission reaches the broker double exactly once.

Given the probe reports an instrument stale, a paper submission for it through dispatch_order returns MARKET_DATA_STALE, reaches no simulation port and creates no IB order; after the probe reports fresh, the next paper submission is accepted by the simulation port.

Through the shipped composition (LineFreshnessBoard + BoardFreshnessProbe + ExecutionEngine::dispatch_order + WiredPaperSimulation + IbBrokerageBridge over a recording gateway), with fixture market data and an injected clock: a subscribed line that never ticked or has been silent for more than 15 s blocks both the designated live strategy's order and a paper strategy's order with MARKET_DATA_STALE and creates no IB order and no resting paper order; after a tick, the next live order reaches the IB bridge exactly once and the next paper order rests in the VirtualOrderBook.

With SRS-MD-003's monitor fed by a real IB paper-gateway subscription, holding the feed for longer than 15 s makes live and paper submissions return MARKET_DATA_STALE, and restoring it makes the next submissions succeed.
Verify acceptance criteria: While subscribed market data is stale, live and paper order submissions return MARKET_DATA_STALE; submissions resume when fresh data is received.

completion_evidence: tools/evidence.py run SRS-MD-004 --obligation C1|C2|C3|C4 -- <the listed test>, each exit 0 at the evidenced commit
an approving tools/adversarial_review.py round at that commit (the reviewer receives this contract)
agent_pool.py integrate SRS-MD-004 --mode implemented, which re-runs C1-C4 itself
limitations: C3 proves acceptance by the simulation port, not a simulated fill: WiredPaperSimulation accepts and rests orders, and the fill loop behind it is SRS-SIM-002/003/004. C4 shows the real PaperSimulationEngine accepting and resting the order.

No production producer feeds a LineFreshnessBoard yet. The live execution host's IB tier stays refused until SRS-EXE-001 composes the SRS-MD-003 feed loop into a board; dispatch_order's current callers are fixture-tier scenarios.
Option lines always read Stale: a SecurityKey cannot carry an option contract identity yet (SRS-MD-001 / SRS-DATA-004).
I1 needs an operator-gated IB paper-gateway window and is not a component criterion.
